name: Live Build Challenge — vibe coding workshop at NEOMA
description: A free 3-hour workshop at NEOMA Business School in Reims to introduce students to vibe coding and the rise of no-code: find a local business that needs a website, build it a redesign with Lovable, then pitch it to the owner. Co-organised with two friends.
context: Most business students have never built software. The goal of the Live Build Challenge was to show them that this has changed: with AI-assisted "vibe coding" tools, describing what you want in plain language is enough to get a working website, which opens product building to non-developers.
The event took place on 2 April 2026, from 2 to 6 pm, at NEOMA Business School in Reims. Entry was free and no technical background was required. I organised it with two friends.

work.title: 3 hours, 3 steps, 1 business
work.text: The challenge followed a real freelance sales cycle, one hour per step.
points: Hunting (1 hour): search Google Maps to find a local business that needs a website.
Build (1 hour): with 100 Lovable credits provided, generate a professional redesign with AI, without writing code.
Pitch (1 hour): contact the owner with immediate proof of value, the site already built.

work.title: My role
work.text: A shared organisation with two friends, where I covered several parts.
points: Set up the room and the equipment.
Led the first part of the workshop: the opening presentation and facilitation.
Acted as technical assistant during the build, explaining technical details and answering participants' questions.

work.title: What students saw in practice
work.text: Beyond the visual result, the demos showed what the tool produces under the hood: a real code base with components, assets and SEO tags (title, description, Open Graph, structured data), and features such as a booking system that need a back end to go live.

work.title: Key takeaway
work.text: No-code and AI tools turn an idea into a usable prototype in an afternoon. The value moves to choosing the right problem, writing clear instructions and judging the result.
